question: When any key or value inside opaque `channelData` contains protected internal runtime context, should OpenClaw drop the entire provider payload or preserve independently safe siblings?
rationale: Both behaviors encode different leakage and delivery guarantees, and existing history and tests do not establish which permanent contract maintainers intend for opaque channel-native payloads.

options.title: Drop the whole payload
options.body: Fail closed by removing all `channelData` when any protected fragment is detected, maximizing leakage safety at the cost of unrelated native content.

options.title: Preserve safe siblings
options.body: Remove only protected branches and retain remaining provider data, preserving more delivery behavior but requiring stronger structural and channel-specific safety proof.

recommendation.title: Drop the whole payload
recommendation.body: Fail closed by removing all `channelData` when any protected fragment is detected, maximizing leakage safety at the cost of unrelated native content.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged interactive and Slack channelData work makes this the strongest available owner for the opaque-payload contract.
